The incidence of Grade 3/4 PRAEs ≤6 months (95% confidence interval [CI]) was 19.8% (12.9-28.5): Child-Pugh B7/B8, 18.2% (8.2-32.7); ECOG PS 2, 19.1% (9.1-33.3); and Vp4, 25.0% (8.7-49.1). ORR (95% CI) was 14.4% (8.5-22.4): Child-Pugh B7/B8, 6.8% (1.4-18.7); ECOG PS 2, 21.3% (10.7-35.7); and Vp4, 15.0% (3.2-37.9).
sections.conclusion: SIERRA safety and efficacy findings were indicative of a favourable risk-benefit profile for STRIDE in this participant population with a high unmet need.

items.title: Lipid Burden and Efficacy of Preventive PCI of Vulnerable Atherosclerotic Coronary Plaques: Post Hoc Analysis From the PREVENT Trial.

sections.objective: Preventive percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of non-flow-limiting lesions (fractional flow reserve >0.80) that are high-risk plaques has emerged as a potential strategy to reduce cardiac events. However, identifying which lesions derive the greatest benefit from preventive PCI compared with optimal medical therapy alone remains challenging. This post hoc analysis evaluates the role of the near-infrared spectroscopy-derived lipid core burden index in identifying high-risk plaques that may benefit from preventive PCI.
sections.methods: Among the 1606 patients enrolled in the PREVENT trial (Preventive Coronary Intervention on Stenosis with Functionally Insignificant Vulnerable Plaque) from September 2015 to September 2021, an investigator-initiated, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, this post hoc analysis included 598 patients (mean age, 64.1±8.8 years; 27.9% women) comprising 632 lesions with a plaque burden >70% and a minimal lumen area 2 by intravascular ultrasound in whom near-infrared spectroscopy evaluation was also performed. Lipid-rich plaque (LRP) was prespecified as having a maximum lipid core burden index over a 4-mm segment >315. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable or progressive angina.
sections.results: LRPs were present in 223 patients (37.3%) with 234 lesions. During median follow-up of 5.6 years, primary outcome events occurred more frequently in patients with LRPs than in those with non-LRPs (12.5% versus 4.7%; unadjusted hazard ratio, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.03-4.19; P =0.039) in the overall population. Within the LRP group, preventive PCI was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome compared with optimal medical therapy alone (7.3% vs. 17.6%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.13-0.41; P P =0.97). A significant interaction was found between treatment strategy and the presence of LRP ( P interaction <0.001).
sections.conclusion: In this post hoc analysis of the PREVENT trial, preventive PCI was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome in patients with near-infrared spectroscopy-defined LRPs, whereas no significant association was observed in those with non-LRPs despite their large plaque burden and small minimal lumen area. These findings suggest the importance of plaque composition, beyond morphological severity alone, in guiding preventive PCI.

items.title: Incidence, Process of Care, and Outcomes of In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in China: A Multicenter Prospective Registry Study.

sections.objective: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is an acute event associated with high mortality. Although survival has improved in high-income countries, contemporary multicenter data from low- and middle-income countries remain scarce, limiting global benchmarking and the identification of system-level opportunities for improvement.
sections.methods: This cohort study used data from the BASIC-IHCA (Baseline Investigation of In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest) registry. Adult patients (≥18 years) who experienced IHCA and received cardiopulmonary resuscitation between July 1, 2019, and December 31, 2020, at 37 hospitals across 29 provinces in China were included. The primary outcome was survival to 30 days or hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation, 6- and 12-month survival, and favorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score 1-2). Process measures focused on the timeliness of resuscitation response and the implementation of postresuscitation interventions.
sections.results: Among 17 602 patients (median age, 66 years; 65.5% male), the annual incidence of adult IHCA was 4.1 per 1000 admissions. Cardiac etiology was identified in 6569 (37.3%) patients, and 2380 (13.5%) presented with initial shockable rhythm. Among all patients, 16 872 (95.9%) received cardiopulmonary resuscitation within 1 minute; timely defibrillation or epinephrine was achieved in 71.4% and 84.4% of patients with initial shockable and nonshockable rhythms, respectively. Sustained return of spontaneous circulation was achieved in 6200 (35.2%) patients, of whom 222 (3.6%) received temperature control therapy and 320 (5.2%) underwent coronary angiography. Overall, 1610 (9.1%) patients survived to 30 days or discharge, with 1241 (7.1%) having a favorable neurological outcome. At 12 months, 1075 (6.1%) patients remained alive, and 986 (5.6%) had a favorable neurological outcome.
sections.conclusion: This multicenter registry highlights a substantial burden of IHCA in China, with markedly low survival rates. Despite prompt initial resuscitation, critical gaps persist in postresuscitation care. Systemic and cultural factors, including the infrequent use of do not attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation orders, may further contribute to survival disparities. These findings suggest several system-level opportunities to improve IHCA outcomes, including structured response systems, optimized critical care resource allocation, and greater integration of advanced care planning.

items.title: The Oxidized Phospholipid PGPC Impairs Angiogenesis by Inhibiting Endothelial Autophagosomal-Lysosomal Fusion Through NPC1-Induced Syntaxin 17 Acetylation and Ubiquitination.

sections.objective: Angiogenesis is essential for the recovery of ischemic hearts with coronary artery disease (CAD). PGPC (1-palmitoyl-2-glutamyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine) is a major phospholipid oxidation product in atherosclerotic lesions. Autophagy participates in angiogenesis. However, whether PGPC affects angiogenesis in ischemic hearts by regulating autophagy remains unclear.
sections.methods: Plasma PGPC concentrations were quantified and the effects of PGPC on angiogenesis were evaluated in cultured endothelial cells and in vivo using a subcutaneous Matrigel plug assay, as well as in hindlimb ischemia and myocardial infarction models in C57BL/6J mice. Autophagic flux and the expression and modification of proteins associated with autophagy and angiogenesis were also assessed.
sections.results: Plasma PGPC levels were increased in patients with CAD, and they were positively correlated with the severity of CAD and negatively correlated with coronary collateral artery formation. PGPC inhibited endothelial cell migration and tube formation. PGPC suppressed neovascularization in Matrigel plugs and reduced blood flow recovery in hindlimb ischemia. In a mouse model of myocardial infarction, PGPC attenuated angiogenesis in the ischemic myocardium. These proangiogenic effects induced by VEGFA (vascular endothelial growth factor A) in ischemic hearts were significantly inhibited by PGPC. Mechanistically, PGPC inhibited the expression of STX17 (syntaxin 17), a crucial molecule that controls autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion by promoting the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitination and degradation of STX17. PGPC upregulated the expression of NPC1 (NPC intracellular cholesterol transporter 1) through CD36 (cluster of differentiation 36). NPC1 not only promoted the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitination and degradation of STX17 through the recruitment of ACAT1 (acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase 1), but also competed with STX17 to bind VAMP8 (vesicle-associated membrane protein 8), leading to inhibition of the expression of eNOS (endothelial nitric oxide synthase), ERK1/2 (extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2), and nitric oxide production. Oxidized phospholipid-neutralizing antibody E06, STX17 overexpression, or silencing of NPC1 reversed the inhibitory effect of PGPC on angiogenesis by restoring autophagic flux.
sections.conclusion: PGPC promotes the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitin-mediated degradation of STX17 by increasing NPC1, leading to a reduction in the level of STX17 associated with VAMP8, which inhibits autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion and angiogenesis. Targeting PGPC, NPC1, or STX17 may represent novel therapeutic approaches to promote angiogenesis in patients with CAD.

items.title: Restenosis after Carotid Artery Stenting in Radiation-induced versus Atherosclerotic Carotid Stenosis: 25-year experience from a tertiary hospital.

sections.objective: To compare the long-term in-stent restenosis (ISR) rate following carotid artery stenting (CAS) in patients with carotid stenosis secondary to atherosclerosis (AS) and radiation-induced stenosis (RIS).
sections.methods: A retrospective review was conducted on 140 CAS procedures in 126 patients at our institution over a 25-year period. Patients with prior neck irradiation were classified as RIS, while the remaining were categorized as AS. Propensity score matching was employed to balance baseline characteristics between the groups. Restenosis was evaluated using specific duplex ultrasound velocity criteria validated for stented arteries. Rates of moderate (≥50%) and severe (≥70%) in-stent restenosis were compared, and long-term restenosis-free survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Multivariate logistic regression was used to determine independent risk factors for ISR.
sections.results: After matching, 40 CAS procedures were included in each group (RIS and AS). Median follow-up duration was 72 months. The RIS group exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of ≥50% ISR (40% vs. 12.5%; p=0.005) and a composite endpoint of ≥50% ISR or new stenosis outside the stented segment (55% vs. 17.5%; p<0.001). The estimated 2-year ISR-free survival at ≥50% was 75.5% in RIS compared to 94.8% in AS (p=0.005). Multivariate analysis identified prior neck irradiation as the sole independent risk factor for ≥50% ISR (OR 7.05, 95% CI 1.26-39.45, p=0.026). No significant risk factors were found for ≥70% ISR. Era-based analysis demonstrated a significant decrease in the incidence of ≥50% and ≥70% ISR in the RIS group during the more recent period, accompanied by shifts in baseline characteristics such as prevalence of hyperlipidema and statin use. Reintervention rate and late ipsilateral neurological events were comparable between the groups.
sections.conclusion: Radiation-induced carotid stenosis is associated with higher rates of long-term moderate (≥50%) in-stent restenosis following carotid artery stenting compared with atherosclerotic disease. However, reintervention and late ipsilateral neurological event rates remain comparable between groups. Recent temporal declines in restenosis coincide with increased statin use and optimized hyperlipidemia management.

items.title: Development and Internal Validation of the Si-AAA Prognostic Score for Five-Year Overall Survival after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair in Patients with Asymptomatic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.

sections.objective: Although endovascular aneurysm repair is widely used for the treatment of asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm, long-term survival is influenced by patient comorbidities and aneurysm-related characteristics. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic scoring system for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair.
sections.methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in patients with asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing endovascular aneurysm repair. Candidate predictors included demographic, clinical, aneurysm-related, and laboratory variables. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent predictors of 5-year mortality. Continuous predictors were categorized using clinically interpretable thresholds derived from time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and a simplified point-based score was constructed from regression coefficients. Model performance was assessed using Harrell's concordance index, and internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples to obtain an optimism-corrected concordance index. Calibration was evaluated using bootstrap-based calibration plots.
sections.results: A total of 445 patients were screened, and 443 complete cases were included in the final analysis. During follow-up, 133 deaths (30.0%) occurred. The estimated 5-year overall survival rate was 62.8% (95% CI, 57.8%-68.0%). Independent predictors of 5-year mortality included age >70 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.66, 95% CI 1.06-2.62; P = .029), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.08-2.69; P = .023), unfit status (aHR 2.32, 95% CI 1.58-3.39; P < .001), serum albumin ≤3.5 g/dL (aHR 2.80, 95% CI 1.97-3.98; P < .001), and abdominal aortic aneurysm diameter ≥7 cm (aHR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.38; P = .023). The final score ranged from 0 to 7. The apparent concordance index was 0.721, with an optimism-corrected concordance index of 0.713 after bootstrap validation. Risk stratification showed clear separation between low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (5-year overall survival: 82.5%, 53.4%, and 23.8%, respectively; log-rank P < .001).
sections.conclusion: A simple prognostic scoring system incorporating age, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unfit status, serum albumin, and aneurysm diameter demonstrated acceptable discrimination and good calibration for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. This tool may assist in risk stratification and long-term clinical decision-making. As this score was derived and internally validated in a single-center cohort, external validation in independent cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

items.title: Association of Race and Socioeconomic Status with Hemodialysis Arteriovenous Access Outcomes.

sections.objective: Arteriovenous access is essential for long-term hemodialysis. The creation and maintenance of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) or arteriovenous graft (AVG) are critical for effective dialysis and minimizing complications. However, the influence of race and social determinants of health on presentation, management, and outcomes has not been well evaluated. This study uses the Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database to evaluate disparities in vascular access outcomes by race and community-level disadvantage.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective study using the VQI database to identify adults who underwent AVF or AVG creation for hemodialysis between 2016 and 2023. The Area Deprivation Index (ADI), a validated measure of neighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage incorporating income, education, employment, and housing quality, was categorized into quartiles from least (Q1) to most disadvantaged (Q4). Patients without follow-up data, recorded complications, or ADI information were excluded. Predisposing factors and postoperative outcomes considering race and ADI were analyzed. Group comparisons were performed using chi-square tests and t-tests. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates was used to assess associations. All analyses were conducted using SPSS version 30.
sections.results: A total of 77,544 patients were included (mean age 62.2 years, 43.4% female). White patients represented the largest racial group (51.5%, n=39,959), and 29.5% (n=22,850) were from the most disadvantaged ADI quartile. AVF maturation was more delayed in White vs Black patients (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI: 1.21-1.70, p<0.001). Immediate postoperative bleeding was less common in White vs Black patients (0.6% vs 0.9%; OR 0.58,0.43-0.79, p<0.001) and less frequent in Q4 vs Q1 (0.5% vs 1.2%; OR 0.36, 0.25-0.53, p<0.001). At 9 months, access patency was lower in Black vs White patients (86.4% vs 88.2%, p=0.003) and varied by ADI (p<0.001), with Q1 achieving the highest patency (88.7%). Nine-month mortality was highest in White patients (28% vs 21% in Black, p<0.001 unadjusted); however, only Asian race remained independently protective after adjustment (OR 0.41, 0.35-0.47, p<0.001 vs Black). Patients in Q4 had significantly higher 9-month mortality compared to Q1 (adjusted OR 1.56, 1.46-1.67, p<0.001).
sections.conclusion: Significant disparities in hemodialysis access outcomes exist by race and socioeconomic status. Patients in disadvantaged areas experienced higher rates of maturation delay and mortality. Black and American Indian/Alaskan Native patients had worse patency and greater AVG use. Structural and social factors strongly influence vascular access outcomes, underscoring the need for targeted interventions to improve equity in hemodialysis care.

items.title: RSV prefusion F vaccine effectiveness in older adults with immunosuppression: a prespecified analysis of the DAN-RSV trial.

sections.objective: Individuals with immunosuppression are at an increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a bivalent RSV prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in older adults (≥60 years) according to immunosuppression status.
sections.methods: This study was a prespecified subgroup analysis of a pragmatic, open-label, nationwide randomised clinical trial conducted in Denmark during November-December, 2024. Older adults were randomised 1:1 to a single dose of RSVpreF or no vaccine. Immunosuppression was defined as at least one hospital encounter with an immunosuppressive condition or treatment. Baseline characteristics and outcomes were ascertained from nationwide registries. The primary outcome was hospitalisation for RSV-related respiratory tract disease, defined as respiratory hospitalisation with an RSV diagnosis code or a positive RSV test. Follow-up began 14 days after the scheduled study visit and continued until May 31, 2025.
sections.results: Among the 131 276 participants (65 642 RSVpreF; 65 634 no vaccine), 5199 (4·0%) were immunosuppressed. In total, 21 participants were hospitalised with RSV-related respiratory tract disease, seven with immunosuppression, and 14 without immunosuppression. In the no-vaccine group, the incidence of RSV-related respiratory tract disease hospitalisation was more than nine-fold higher in participants with immunosuppression than in participants without (4·68 vs 0·50 events per 1000 person-years). As previously shown, RSVpreF significantly reduced RSV-related respiratory tract disease hospitalisations in the overall population (vaccine effectiveness 83·3% [95% CI 42·9 to 96·9]). No significant effect modification by immunosuppression status was observed (vaccine effectiveness 60·5% [95% CI -141·4 to 96·2] among those with immunosuppression and 92·3% [48·7 to 99·8] among those without immunosuppression; p for interaction=0·22). The point estimate was numerically lower among participants with immunosuppression, with a wide confidence interval crossing the null, but there was no statistical evidence of heterogeneity between subgroups. The estimated absolute rate reduction was 2·83 events per 1000 person-years (95% CI -2·00 to 7·66) among the participants with immunosuppression and 0·46 events per 1000 person-years (0·18 to 0·74) among those without immunosuppression.
sections.conclusion: In adults aged 60 years or older, RSVpreF vaccination reduced hospitalisations for RSV-related respiratory tract disease with no statistical evidence of effect modification by immunosuppression status; however, the study was not powered to exclude subgroup differences. Given the higher baseline risk of RSV-related hospitalisation observed among the individuals with immunosuppression, prioritising RSV vaccination in this group with high risk of severe RSV disease could have clinical benefits. The results of this trial could help to inform clinical guidance and vaccination policy, pending confirmation in larger studies.

items.title: Mental health and urinary incontinence in childhood.
items.abstract: Intermittent and uncontrolled loss of urine is common among children but requires medical attention when it persists beyond age 5 years. Mostly functional in origin, urinary incontinence is caused by a complex inter-relationship of biopsychosocial factors, and evidence shows that mental health problems and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are common in children and adolescents with urinary incontinence. Mental health problems and ACEs (including abuse, neglect, and household dysfunction) could be both causes and consequences of paediatric urinary incontinence, but research is needed to understand causal pathways. Treatment guidelines increasingly recognise the need to integrate assessment of psychosocial factors and mental health support into clinical care pathways for children affected by urinary incontinence. Parental and societal beliefs, cultural norms, availability of sanitation facilities, economic constraints, and policy-level gaps affect the management of paediatric urinary incontinence. Early assessment and treatment are needed to prevent urinary incontinence from becoming chronic and negatively impacting on children's quality of life, wellbeing, and education.

items.title: Decoding systemic vascular health and hypertensive disorders in pregnancy through retinal imaging and Visionary AI.
items.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy arise from early placental and systemic vascular dysfunction, yet current first-trimester screening remains imprecise, biologically opaque and logistically challenging. Here we present Visionary AI, an interpretable platform that integrates retinal imaging with graph-based vascular modeling to predict hypertensive disorders before clinical onset. Visionary AI converts retinal images into topological and geometric representations of microvascular structure, enabling risk prediction from biologically grounded vascular features rather than generic image embeddings or clinical variables. In a prospective development cohort of 1,267 pregnancies, Visionary AI achieved strong performance for preeclampsia across population-wide control settings (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.91, average precision (AP) = 0.81). A stability-optimized model transferred without retraining to an independent external validation cohort, achieving AUC = 0.81 and AP = 0.68 and outperforming clinical and deep learning benchmarks. Recurrent features involving retinal vascular topology, geometry, network complexity and hierarchical organization position the maternal retina as a minimally invasive biosensor of systemic vascular health and Visionary AI as a biologically interpretable framework for pregnancy risk stratification.

items.title: MK-4002, a B-cell maturation antigen-targeting T-cell engager, in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma: a first-in-human, open-label, phase 1 study.

sections.objective: The optimal treatment strategy for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma remains unclear. This first-in-human study aimed to evaluate the safety, preliminary activity, and pharmacokinetics of the trispecific B-cell maturation antigen-targeting T-cell engager MK-4002 in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.
sections.methods: This open-label, phase 1 study was conducted at 12 sites (hospitals and cancer centres) in France, Spain, and the USA. Participants were aged 18 years or older, had relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 0 to 2, and had received at least three previous therapies. Participants received MK-4002 at doses from 0·005 mg to 24 mg intravenously weekly or every 2 weeks following a dose escalation design. One participant was enrolled per dose level, starting at 0·005 mg. Once an adverse event of grade 2 or worse or a dose-limiting toxicity was observed, the study transitioned to a 3 + 3 dose escalation phase. Initially, dose escalation occurred in fixed-dose cohorts (target dose weekly on day 1 of each cycle). Once a grade 2 or worse cytokine release syndrome event occurred, step-up dosing began (treatment initiated with at least one priming dose on day 1 of cycle 1 followed by the target dose weekly or every 2 weeks). Dose escalation continued until the maximum tolerated dose (MTD), recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D), or both, were identified. Expansion cohorts of up to 15 participants were added to assess regimens and schedules at dose levels considered safe by the Cohort Review Committee. Primary endpoints were safety; MTD, RP2D, or both; and pharmacokinetics. The key secondary endpoint was overall response rate (ORR) per International Myeloma Working Group criteria. Safety was analysed in all participants who received at least one dose of MK-4002. ORR was analysed in all participants who received at least one dose of MK-4002 and had at least one postbaseline disease assessment. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04184050) and is ongoing but closed to recruitment.
sections.results: Between April 21, 2020, and June 28, 2023, 97 participants were enrolled and treated across 17 fixed-dose, stepped-dose, and dose-expansion cohorts. Median age was 69 years (IQR 61-74); 50 participants (52%) were male and 47 (48%) female. Median time since diagnosis was 6·8 years (IQR 4·2-9·9), and participants had received a median of six (IQR 4-8) previous lines of therapy. Median time from first dose to data cutoff was 27·1 months (IQR 15·7-34·3). Dose-limiting toxicities occurred in six participants. The MTD for the fixed dose was established as 2·15 mg and was not reached in the stepped-dose cohorts. Adverse events occurred in 97 participants (100%); 77 (79%) had grade 3 or worse events. The most common grade 3 or worse adverse events were anaemia (33 participants [34%]), neutrophil count decreased (22 participants [23%]), and neutropenia (18 participants [19%]). Serious adverse events occurred in 56 participants (58%). One participant (1%) died due to treatment-related traumatic subdural haematoma. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 29 participants (30%): grade 1-2 occurred in 27 participants, and grade 3 occurred in two participants (both after a 24 mg dose). MK-4002 exhibited dose-proportional pharmacokinetics with a median half-life of 68 h (range 52-76). ORR was 41% (95% CI 22-61) in the 2·15-6 mg dose group (nine of 27 participants had a very good partial response or better), 63% (38-84) in the 12 mg group (ten of 19 participants had a very good partial response or better), and 48% (31-67) in the 24 mg dose group (12 of 33 participants had a very good partial response or better). Taking safety and activity results together, a target dose of 12 mg was identified as the preliminary RP2D.
sections.conclusion: MK-4002 had manageable safety and clinical activity at doses of 2·15 mg or higher in participants with heavily pretreated relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Optimal safety and activity were observed at 12 mg, supporting further clinical evaluation of this dose.

items.title: Future-proofing thalassaemia care: harnessing scalable therapies, artificial intelligence, and global collaboration.
items.abstract: Advances in the treatment of thalassaemia have led to major improvements in survival and quality of life over the past 30 years. In addition to developments in stem-cell transplantation, transfusion safety, iron overload monitoring, and iron-chelation therapy, novel disease-modifying and gene therapies are also emerging. However, substantial disparities in access to specialised care and novel therapies persist, particularly in low-income and middle-income countries, where most people with thalassaemia reside. This Series paper explores complementary strategies aimed at improving global thalassaemia outcomes beyond conventional therapeutic innovation. We discuss the emerging role of repurposed low-cost therapies, particularly hydroxyurea and thalidomide, as disease-modifying options in resource-limited settings. We further examine opportunities to democratise access to curative gene therapies through technological developments, decentralised manufacturing, regional collaborations, and simplified treatment platforms. In addition, the rapidly expanding role of artificial intelligence in screening, diagnosis, prediction of complications, and remote care delivery is reviewed. Finally, we highlight the importance of international collaborations, multidisciplinary training, and research networks in strengthening equitable global thalassaemia care.

items.title: The expanding therapeutic landscape of β-thalassaemia.
items.abstract: β-thalassaemia is characterised by ineffective erythropoiesis, chronic anaemia, haemolysis, and progressive iron-related and non-iron-related morbidity. Although transfusion, iron chelation, multidisciplinary care, and allogeneic haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation have substantially improved outcomes, major gaps persist in treatment burden, access, safety, adherence, and curative feasibility. Over the past decade, the therapeutic landscape has expanded rapidly, with disease-modifying agents targeting erythroid maturation and red cell metabolism, including luspatercept and mitapivat, now available as options for both transfusion-dependent and non-transfusion-dependent β-thalassaemia. In parallel, gene addition and gene editing therapies, particularly beti-cel and exa-cel, have established proof of curative potential independent of donor availability. However, optimal patient selection, response definitions, long-term outcome assessment, affordability, and equitable global access remain central challenges for wide implementation. In this Series paper, we discuss advances in β-thalassaemia treatment over the past decade, including newly approved and late-stage therapies and their future implications, and highlight remaining research gaps.

items.title: Safety, antiviral activity, and pharmacokinetics of long-acting cabotegravir plus long-acting rilpivirine in virologically suppressed adolescents living with HIV-1 (IMPAACT 2017/MOCHA): week 96 and end-of-study results from a multinational, phase 1/2, single-arm trial.

sections.objective: Week 24 and week 48 study data from the International Maternal Pediatric Adolescent AIDS Clinical Trials Network (IMPAACT 2017)/More Options for Children and Adolescents (MOCHA) trial supported the use of long-acting cabotegravir plus long-acting rilpivirine, given every 4 weeks or 8 weeks, per the adult dosing regimens, in adolescents who were virologically suppressed. Having reached the end of the trial, we report the safety, acceptability and tolerability, antiviral activity, and pharmacokinetics of these drugs in adolescents at 96 weeks.
sections.methods: In this phase 1/2 non-comparative trial, adolescents (aged 12-17 years, weighing ≥35 kg) with HIV-1 who were virologically suppressed were enrolled across 18 sites in Botswana, South Africa, Thailand, Uganda, and the USA. Participants switched from pre-study antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 4 weeks of daily oral cabotegravir plus oral rilpivirine, followed by 600 mg long-acting cabotegravir plus 900 mg long-acting rilpivirine intramuscular (3 mL each) injections at weeks 4 and 8, and then every 8 weeks through to week 96. There was an optional extension phase of up to 48 weeks to transition to open-label medications or a continued drug access programme, as applicable, based on in-country approval. The 96-week objectives were to evaluate the safety, antiviral and immunological activity of long-acting cabotegravir plus long-acting rilpivirine in adolescents living with HIV, evaluate tolerability and acceptability, and characterise long-term safety and washout pharmacokinetics through to 96 weeks. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03497676, and is complete.
sections.results: Between July 26, 2021, and Aug 27, 2022, 144 participants enrolled (median age at study enrolment 15 years [IQR 14-16]; 74 [51%] of 144 female; 106 [74%] of 144 Black or African American). Three participants were lost to follow-up and six prematurely discontinued study treatment (one treatment non-compliance, one eligibility criteria violation, one drug-related adverse event, and three for pregnancy). Median total-exposure duration was 128 weeks (IQR 113-136). Through to week 96, 35 of 144 participants had an adverse event of grade 3 or higher (24% [95% CI 17·6-32·2]); three had a drug-related adverse event of grade 3 or higher (2% [0·4-6·0]). There were no confirmed virological failures through to week 96. Median (5-95th percentile) week 96 observed trough concentrations of cabotegravir (2·96 μg/mL [1·40-5·52]) and rilpivirine (89·5 ng/mL [54·1-152·0]) approximated those in adults. Through to week 96, at least 97% of participants on treatment preferred injectable treatment to daily oral treatment. No grade 3 or higher drug-related adverse events or confirmed virological failures occurred after week 96.
sections.conclusion: 96-week study data show sustained safety and antiviral activity, favourable pharmacokinetics, and good acceptability and tolerability in adolescents living with HIV who were virologically suppressed, inform the growing global approvals, and support the ongoing clinical use of injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine in this age group.

items.title: Three-year outcomes of combined surgical peripheral iridectomy, goniosynechialysis and goniotomy for advanced primary angle-closure glaucoma: a multicentre study.

sections.objective: To assess the 3-year efficacy and safety of combined surgical peripheral iridectomy (SPI), goniosynechialysis (GSL) and goniotomy (GT) for advanced primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG) without cataract.
sections.methods: This was a multicentre prospective observational study with extended follow-up. We enrolled advanced PACG without cataract patients who underwent combined SPI+GSL+ GT and completed 36-month follow-up. Key outcomes included changes in intraocular pressure (IOP), best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), usage of anti-glaucoma medications, surgical success rates, progression of peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS), endothelial cell density, visual field (VF) mean deviation (MD) and long-term postoperative complications.
sections.results: A total of 70 eyes from 58 patients were included in the final analysis. Baseline mean IOP (29.4±8.1 mm Hg) decreased to 16.4±4.01 mm Hg at 36 months (40.7±18.8% reduction, p<0.001), with anti-glaucoma medications declining from 2.0±1.4 to 0.7±0.9 (p<0.001), representing a 65.7% reduction in required medications postoperatively. At the 3-year follow-up, the cumulative complete and qualified success rates were 54.3% and 84.3%, respectively. Median BCVA worsened slightly (0.00 vs 0.10 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution, p<0.001); 21.4% of eyes had significant vision loss (≥2 Snellen lines), attributable to cataract progression. MD of VF remained stable (p=0.217). Main late complications were cataract requiring surgery (n=10) and persistent PAS (n=11), with no vision-threatening events. Older age correlated with higher 3-year surgical success (p<0.05).
sections.conclusion: Combined SPI+GSL+GT provides sustained IOP reduction, stable visual function, and a favourable safety profile over 3 years, supporting its role as a reliable long-term treatment for advanced PACG without cataract.

items.title: Endphthalmitis after cataract surgery in Sweden 2018-2024: associations with preoperative visual acuity and intracameral antibiotic regimens.

sections.objective: Cataract surgery is one of the world's most common and successful procedures. Postoperative endophthalmitis (PE) is rare but may be devastating. This study investigated associations between preoperative visual acuity (VA), other patient-related and surgery-related characteristics and PE. As a secondary objective, outcomes associated with the most commonly used intracameral antibiotic regimens were explored.
sections.methods: This retrospective cohort study used data from the population-based Swedish National Cataract Register from 2018 to 2024.
sections.results: Among 979 534 procedures, PE incidence was 0.013% (131 cases). In a multivariate analysis, male sex, ocular comorbidity and capsule complication showed higher ORs for PE while preoperative VA≥20/40 and immediate sequential bilateral surgery showed lower ORs for PE. Patients with better preoperative VA were younger and had fewer ocular comorbidities, intraoperative challenges and complications, indicating a more favourable case mix.Endophthalmitis rates varied by intracameral antibiotic regimen: 0.017% with cefuroxime alone, 0.011% with cefuroxime plus ampicillin and 0.010% with moxifloxacin. No regimen demonstrated statistically significant superiority. Enterococci occurred more frequently with cefuroxime. Time to PE diagnosis was longer with combination therapy and moxifloxacin versus cefuroxime alone. Visual outcomes were generally poor (48%<20/200), but moxifloxacin cases achieved≥20/40 final VA more often than cefuroxime (50% vs 23%).
sections.conclusion: PE incidence was very low. Better preoperative VA and immediate sequential bilateral cataract surgery were associated with lower observed odds, probably reflecting favourable case mix and residual confounding rather than causal protection. No IC antibiotic regimen was independently associated with lower PE incidence.

items.title: Exacerbation trajectories in biologic-eligible severe asthma patients.

sections.objective: Asthma biologics are highly effective in reducing exacerbations. Improvement in exacerbations after biologic initiation is often attributed to treatment effect. What proportion of biologic-eligible severe asthma patients improve without biologic therapy, and what characterises those who remain frequent exacerbators?
sections.methods: Biologic-naïve adults with severe asthma were identified in nationwide UK electronic medical records. Year 0 was defined as the first year patients met severe asthma criteria with ≥3 systemic corticosteroid-treated exacerbations (biologic-eligible). Post-eligibility exacerbation trajectories were identified using longitudinal k-means. Sensitivity analyses included alternative k and a lower exacerbation threshold (≥2/year). Covariates included the highest blood eosinophil count, inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) dose and comorbidities.
sections.results: Among 10,078 biologic-eligible adults (median age 51 years; 71% female), we identified three exacerbation trajectories: (1) Remitting-stable (70%, n=7,091), with sustained improvement to 10 courses/year). Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Remitting-stable patients were least likely to have bronchiectasis but were otherwise similar in demographics and allergic comorbidities. Blood eosinophil count was higher in the chronic-frequent group (Year 0 median 0.30×10 9 /L) compared with remitting-stable (0.23×10 9 /L) and refractory-frequent groups (0.21×10 9 /L, p<0.001); this was evident several years before meeting biologic exacerbation criteria.
sections.conclusion: Over two-thirds of biologic-eligible patients improved with standard care alone. Chronic-frequent exacerbators had higher blood eosinophil counts, even years before meeting biologic criteria, suggesting a distinct disease phenotype.

items.title: From Menarche to Menopause: A Narrative Review of Female Reproductive Milestones and Risk of Chronic Airway Disease.

sections.objective: Female reproductive factors are underrecognized determinants of lifelong respiratory health. This narrative review examines relationships between reproductive milestones and chronic airway disease risk. Female reproductive factors may influence susceptibility to chronic airway disease, although these relationships involve multiple pathways, with obesity as a major confounder. A dedicated life-course cohort with deep phenotyping and hormone profiling is needed to elucidate how reproductive exposures, sex hormones, metabolic determinants and other susceptibility factors interact to shape respiratory outcomes in females.
sections.results: Early menarche is associated with reduced adult lung function and a higher incidence of asthma. Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome is also associated with increased asthma risk, particularly in obese individuals, through sex hormone dysregulation, metabolic dysfunction, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Adverse pregnancy outcomes are associated with lower lung function and heightened future asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) susceptibility, potentially from persistent systemic inflammation, endothelial injury, and oxidative stress beyond the perinatal period. Effects of exogenous sex hormones on the airways are complex and context-dependent. Hormonal contraception may reduce asthma risk in lean females by stabilizing estrogen and progesterone fluctuations, but increase risk in obesity, as exogenous estrogen can amplify airway inflammation. Similarly, effects of menopause hormone therapy (MHT) vary by formulation, timing of initiation, and use duration. Estrogen-only MHT - particularly when started at younger ages, before menopause, or used for longer duration - may increase asthma risk. Early menopause is linked to accelerated lung function decline, higher asthma incidence among those with obesity, and increased COPD risk.

items.title: Primary Melanoma Stage as a Predictor of Survival in Advanced Disease: Findings from the Spanish Melanoma Registry GEM1801.

sections.objective: Systemic relapse after stage I melanoma is uncommon, but accounts for nearly one-third of metastatic melanoma cases. The prognostic impact of primary melanoma stage in advanced disease is unknown.
sections.methods: Overall survival (OS) was analyzed in patients with advanced melanoma from the Spanish Melanoma Registry (2018-2024), stratified by primary stage.
sections.results: Among 365 patients with metastatic melanoma treated at first line, 58 had prior stage I, 32 IIA, 80 IIB/C, and 195 III. Median time to relapse was 52 months for stage I, 30 months in IIA, 27 months in IIB/C and 25 months in stage III (p=0.0001). At systemic relapse, patients with previous stage I more frequently had ≥3 metastatic sites (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.06-3.35), brain metastases (OR 4.02, 95% CI 2.13-7.58), and elevated LDH (OR 2.19, 95% CI 1.18-4.04). Median OS was shorter for patients with prior stage I (19.8 m, 95% CI 12, 55.9) versus stage IIA (60.1 m, 95% CI 52.8, NR), IIB/C (32.6 m, 95% CI 18.9, NR), and III (43 m, 95% CI 25.5, 62.3) (p=0.024).
sections.conclusion: Systemic relapse after stage I melanoma is associated with higher tumor burden and poorer survival than relapse after stage II/III.

items.title: Dragnet.
items.abstract: A 24-year-old previously healthy woman with a high body mass index presented with a several week history of poor vision in the left eye associated with non-positional headaches. Examination was notable for Frisén grade 2 bilateral optic disc swelling with a visual acuity of 20/20-1 in the right eye, 20/100 + 1 in the left eye with no relative afferent pupillary defect. Magnetic resonance (MR) imaging and MR venography of the brain were negative for a mass or venous sinus thrombosis. Lumbar puncture opening pressure was elevated, and the cerebrospinal fluid constituents were bland. A diagnosis of idiopathic intracranial hypertension was made; however, despite improvement in the papilledema with oral acetazolamide the vision continued to be reduced in the left eye. Macular optical coherence tomography confirmed a juxtapapillary choroidal neovascular membrane extending into the macula. The evaluation and various causes of visual loss in the setting of papilledema are discussed.

items.title: Three-dimensional architecture of outer retinal tubulation in Bietti crystalline dystrophy.

sections.objective: To characterize the three-dimensional morphology and cellular-level organization of outer retinal tubulation (ORT) in Bietti crystalline dystrophy (BCD) and to evaluate its structural relationship with the residual outer retina.
sections.methods: Observational case series. Patients with BCD exhibiting ORT were included. ORT and contiguous ORT-associated regions were evaluated three-dimensionally using two complementary approaches: en face optical coherence tomography (OCT) images generated from the innermost ORT boundary to Bruch's membrane, and ellipsoid zone (EZ)-like band-to-Bruch's membrane thickness maps (hereafter referred to as EZ-to-Bruch's membrane thickness maps). Cellular-level ORT organization was further assessed using adaptive optics OCT (AO-OCT). Three-dimensional ORT morphology, spatial relationship between ORT-associated structures and the EZ-like band, EZ-to-Bruch's membrane thickness distribution, and AO-OCT features of ORT wall organization were assessed.
sections.results: Nineteen eyes from 19 patients were included. En face OCT images were analyzable in 15 eyes, and AO-OCT images were analyzable in 9 eyes. The EZ-like band could be traced to the hyperreflective ORT wall in all eyes assessed using en face OCT. En face OCT showed complex ORT-associated planar structures with branching and confluent configurations. EZ-to-Bruch's membrane thickness maps closely corresponded to the contours of these ORT-associated planar structures, suggesting that the maps reflected the overall geometry of the residual outer retina. Peripheral EZ-to-Bruch's membrane thickening was observed in most eyes, and quantitative thickness-distance analysis identified characteristic peripheral peak patterns in eyes with intermediate-sized ORT-associated regions, suggesting that these thickened regions may be associated with ORT formation. AO-OCT showed multiple hyperreflective dots arranged in rosette-like configurations around a central hyporeflective lumen, consistent with presumed photoreceptor nuclei within the ORT wall.
sections.conclusion: ORT in BCD showed complex three-dimensional planar configurations spatially associated with the residual outer retina. These findings suggest that the peripheral margin of the ORT-associated outer retina may represent a key site of structural reorganization and support the concept that ORT in BCD represents a manifestation of outer retinal structural reorganization in the setting of progressive degeneration.

items.title: Effects of MASH risk genotypes on resmetirom efficacy in patients with MASH and fibrosis.

sections.objective: Resmetirom, a thyroid hormone receptor beta agonist, improves metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver fibrosis in patients with non-cirrhotic MASH. Risk genotypes of PNPLA3, HSD17B13, TM6SF2, MTARC1, MBOAT7, and SERPINA1 have been associated with altered susceptibility to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASH, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and/or hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated the impact of MASLD risk genotypes on baseline characteristics and the response to resmetirom vs. placebo with respect to MASH, fibrosis, MRI-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF), and other biomarkers.
sections.methods: Testing the effects of MASLD risk genotypes or combinations of high-risk alleles on liver biopsy, MRI-PDFF, and biomarker responses to resmetirom was a pre-specified analysis in 738 patients enrolled in the MAESTRO-NASH phase III trial who consented to DNA collection, were genotyped for all genes, and had liver biopsies at baseline and Week 52.
sections.results: At baseline, patients with high-risk genotypes of PNPLA3 or HSD17B13 had a lower frequency of metabolic risk factors, including type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, than patients with low-risk genotypes. Interaction analyses and efficacy assessments indicated that resmetirom had similar positive effects on MASH resolution, fibrosis improvement on liver biopsy, MRI-PDFF response, and biomarkers at Week 52 in MAESTRO-NASH patients with high-risk genotypes of PNPLA3, HSD17B13, TM6SF2, MTARC1, and MBOAT7, either individually or as part of a composite genetic risk score. These effects were independent of sex, Hispanic ethnicity, and metabolic risk factors. Due to the limited sample size, the study was not powered to detect small effects of risk genotypes on resmetirom efficacy.
sections.conclusion: Resmetirom's effects on MASH, liver fibrosis, MRI-PDFF, and MASH biomarkers in the MAESTRO-NASH trial were not significantly impacted by the presence of common MASH risk genotypes, suggesting that resmetirom's mechanism of action may help mitigate the deleterious effects of MASH risk variants. Clinical trial Number: NCT03900429 IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Resmetirom has recently been approved for the treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). It leads to MASH resolution and improvement of fibrosis in patients with non-cirrhotic MASH. Patients with MASH have higher prevalence of certain genetic variants which can be associated with more severe disease. In this study we evaluated the relationship between the presence of select MASH risk genotypes (e.g. PNPLA3, TM6SF2, or HSD17B13) or the combined total of MASH genetic risk alleles on the response to resmetirom and placebo in 738 patients with non-cirrhotic MASH with serial liver biopsies at baseline and week 52. Within the limitation of study sample size, resmetirom's benefits on MASH resolution, fibrosis improvement and hepatic steatosis were independent of the presence of MASH genetic risk genotypes either alone or in combination.

items.title: Temporal assessment of spatial and single-cell transcriptomes identifies CD226-NECTIN2 T cell-cholangiocyte interaction in bile duct inflammation.

sections.objective: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) and primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) are inflammatory bile duct disorders affecting mostly young adults that often lead to liver cirrhosis and cancer. Especially for PSC, pathogenic mechanisms remain unclear and treatment options are lacking. To better understand biliary disease processes in bile duct inflammation, we analyzed livers of NOD.c3c4 mice by spatial and single-cell (scRNA-seq) transcriptomics, identifying key cell types, interactions and potential changes over time that were validated in human liver explants. PSC is an intractable immune-mediated cholestatic liver disease that mainly affects young people and has a significant impact on families and the healthcare system due to treatment costs and sick leave. Our study aimed to find new ways of understanding PSC and highlight potential treatment targets by first identifying disease-relevant cell interactions in a mouse model, followed by confirmation in human PSC livers.
sections.methods: Livers of 10, 20 and 40-week-old male NOD.c3c4 mice were used for spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq. Differentially-expressed genes at different time points were analyzed using the CellphoneDB database with a focus on T cell-related interactions. CD226-NECTIN2 interaction was validated using co-culture experiments and antibody treatment in NOD.c3c4 mice. CD226-NECTIN2 in PSC, PBC and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) explants was analyzed by spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence.
sections.results: Spatial transcriptomics consistently distinguished inflamed and non-inflamed liver areas in NOD.c3c4 mice at different ages. When combined with scRNA-seq enriched for immune cells and cholangiocytes, key inflammatory cell types were localized to biliary structures. Using differentially-expressed genes and a curated overview of biologically-validated interactions (CellphoneDB), the CD226-NECTIN2 T cell-cholangiocyte interaction was discovered. Knock-down of Nectin2 in vitro and anti-CD226 blocking in NOD.c3c4 mice specifically reduced T cell activation and diseased human liver showed consistent CD226-NECTIN2 co-localization at inflamed bile ducts.
sections.conclusion: By combining spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq in NOD.c3c4 mice, we generated a pipeline for in-depth identification of potential disease relevant genes and interaction partners. The T cell-cholangiocyte interaction CD226-NECTIN2 was identified, functionally validated and detected in human disease highlighting this interaction as a possible future treatment target.

items.title: Anticancer Drugs and Cancer-Associated Thrombosis.
items.abstract: The rapid development of novel cancer therapies has considerably improved the care of cancer patients and cancer-related survival; however, these therapies are associated with a broad range of adverse events that have become a major burden in this population. Alongside other cancer-related factors, vascular toxicity from anticancer therapies contributes to an increased risk of venous thromboembolism. Among anticancer drugs, chemotherapeutic agents (eg, anthracyclines, platinum-based drugs, antimetabolites), hormonal therapies (eg, selective estrogen receptor modulators), agents used for multiple myeloma (including immunomodulatory drugs and proteasome inhibitors), asparaginase, as well as targeted inhibitors to immune checkpoints, vascular endothelial growth factor, epidermal growth factor receptor, tyrosine kinases, cyclin-dependent kinases, and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase are primarily associated with increased risk of venous thromboembolism. Vascular adverse events associated with anticancer drugs are frequently underestimated, and significant gaps remain in the risk stratification, prevention, and management of thromboembolic events in patients receiving systemic anticancer therapies. This review examines the evidence linking anticancer drug exposure to the incidence of venous thromboembolism, summarizes the key underlying pathobiological mechanisms, and highlights current guideline recommendations for the prevention and treatment of cancer-associated thrombosis. Arterial thrombotic events are also discussed where clinically or mechanistically relevant. This review also offers advanced cardio-oncology perspectives on the identification, risk stratification, and therapeutic targeting of drug-induced vascular toxicity.

items.title: Adverse Remodeling and Fibrosis Predict Outcomes in Excessive Trabeculation of the Left Ventricle: A Multiparametric CMR Risk Score.

sections.objective: Excessive trabeculation of the left ventricle (ETLV) is a heterogeneous and controversial phenotype that overlaps with both physiological remodeling and cardiomyopathy. This study sought to develop and validate a cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-based model to predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and to assess the incremental prognostic value of trabeculation metrics.
sections.methods: In this international retrospective study, 589 patients with ETLV across 17 centers underwent core-laboratory CMR analysis. The composite MACE endpoint included heart failure, ventricular arrhythmia, systemic embolism, or all-cause death. A prediction model was derived from morphofunctional CMR parameters and validated in an independent cohort. The incremental value of trabeculation indices was then assessed. Outcomes were further compared with a propensity-matched cohort of 197 patients with dilated cardiomyopathy.
sections.results: Mean age was 43 ± 18 years, 43% were women, mean left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction was 48% ± 14%, and 12% had late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). Over a median follow-up of 3.6 years, 121 (21%) patients experienced MACE. A model including indexed LV end-diastolic volume, LV global longitudinal strain, and LGE extent demonstrated moderate prognostic performance (C-statistic 0.77 in derivation; 0.70 in validation) and calibration. Addition of trabeculated mass percentage (TM%) modestly improved discrimination (C-statistic 0.79 in derivation, P = 0.012; 0.72 in validation); an exploratory TM% ≥28% identified higher-risk patients. However, TM% was not predictive among individuals with normal indexed LV end-diastolic volume, preserved LV global longitudinal strain, and minimal LGE, who exhibited excellent outcomes. Prognosis was comparable in propensity-matched ETLV and dilated cardiomyopathy cohorts (P = 0.557).
sections.conclusion: CMR-based risk stratification in ETLV is primarily driven by adverse LV remodeling and fibrosis, whereas trabeculation indices provide only modest incremental prognostic value. In the absence of high-risk imaging features, ETLV likely represents a benign morphologic trait. This pragmatic multiparametric CMR score may support clinical decision-making in this debated phenotype.

items.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Anticoagulation Alone in Intermediate-High Risk PE: Improved Functional 90-Day Outcomes in STORM-PE RCT.

sections.objective: Up to 50% of pulmonary embolism (PE) survivors experience long-term functional limitations and reduced quality of life (QoL). Reperfusion strategies can rapidly relieve right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction and prevent clinical deterioration or hemodynamic collapse; however, these approaches have never been evaluated in a randomized trial against anticoagulation alone using patient-centered outcomes. This study sought to evaluate whether mechanical thrombectomy with anticoagulation improves functional, QoL, and safety outcomes compared with anticoagulation alone in patients with acute intermediate-high risk PE over 90 days.
sections.methods: STORM-PE enrolled 100 PE patients randomized 1:1 to computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) with anticoagulation or anticoagulation alone across 22 international sites, with RV-to-left-ventricular (RV/LV) ratio change at 48 hours as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints included major adverse events within 7 days, functional and QoL outcomes, mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence through 90 days.
sections.results: For all patients, median time from randomization to last follow-up visit was 91.0 days [Q1-Q3: 80.5-100.0]. At 90 days, 66.0% (31/47) of CAVT and 64.2% (34/53) of anticoagulation patients completed the 6-min walk test. The CAVT arm exhibited a longer 6-min walk distance compared with anticoagulation alone (478.7 ± 159.5 m vs 368.0 ± 127.8 m, P = 0.003). More CAVT than anticoagulation patients were NYHA Functional Class I (97.4% [37/38] vs 75.6% [34/45], P = 0.005) at 90 days. Dyspnea and QoL scores were comparable between groups, with no differences between arms for all-cause mortality, PE-related mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence within 90 days.
sections.conclusion: In STORM-PE, CAVT with anticoagulation resulted in improved functional outcomes at 90 days compared with anticoagulation alone, with equivalent safety rates. This trial supports CAVT as an effective and safe reperfusion strategy for intermediate-high risk PE.

items.title: Digital technology in everyday life: emerging associations with social, mental, and physical health and wellbeing.
items.abstract: The digital determinants of health refer to digitally mediated factors that increasingly shape lifestyle, behaviour, and social connections. Digital devices, infrastructure, and services-ranging from mobile phones, social media and online games to emerging technologies such as generative artificial intelligence and robotics-have become integral to everyday life in many parts of the world. These technologies are reshaping the way individuals and communities experience social and mental health, facilitating new forms of connection, belonging, and participation. At the same time, these dimensions of health can be threatened by some forms of engagement with these technologies, which might also reinforce existing inequities. In this Viewpoint, we examine the digital determinants of health within a framework of social, mental, and physical health and wellbeing, adopting a public health lens to harness digital technologies for improved health and wellbeing for all people.

items.title: Combined amivantamab, lazertinib, and bevacizumab in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced non-small-cell lung cancer with acquired resistance to a third-generation EGFR tyrosine-kinase inhibitor (ETOP 18-21 AMAZE-lung): a prospective, international, multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: MET and angiogenic pathways are activated in EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) upon resistance to tyrosine-kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Amivantamab, an EGFR and MET bispecific antibody, is approved in combination with chemotherapy for EGFR-mutant NSCLC post-osimertinib progression based on results of the MARIPOSA-2 trial. We assessed the activity and safety of combined amivantanab, lazertinib, and bevacizumab-a chemotherapy-sparing strategy-for patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC and acquired resistance to a third-generation EGFR TKI.
sections.methods: ETOP 18-21 AMAZE-lung was a prospective, international, multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial. Adults (aged ≥18 years) with advanced stage, pathologically confirmed non-squamous NSCLC harbouring a sensitising EGFR mutation (exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R, or both) with disease progression following treatment with a third-generation EGFR TKI (osimertinib or lazertinib) given in the first-line or second-line setting were included. Patients received intravenous amivantamab at a fixed dose of 1400 mg or 1750 mg (if bodyweight ≥80 kg) every 3 weeks for two cycles, then 1750 mg or 2100 mg (if bodyweight ≥80 kg) every 3 weeks from cycle three; oral lazertinib at a daily dose of 240 mg; and bevacizumab at a dose of 15 mg per kg every 3 weeks. Treatment was given until progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary outcome was 12-week objective response rate (defined by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours version 1.1), evaluated in the first 60 patients enrolled (intention-to-treat population). To reject an objective response rate of 20% or less versus 40%, at least 19 responses needed to be observed (2·2% significance level with 93% power). Safety was evaluated in terms of any-cause adverse events and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) graded according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0, assessed in all enrolled patients who received at least one dose of trial treatment. The trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05601973) and in the European Medicines Agency's Clinical Trials Information System (EU CT number 2021-002337-42); the primary analysis is complete but follow-up for patients on treatment is ongoing.
sections.results: Between March 27, 2023, and May 21, 2024, 61 patients were enrolled from 17 sites in Europe. Median age was 65 years (IQR 61-70), and most patients were female (43 [70%]) and White (50 [82%]). 37 (61%) patients had never smoked, 38 (62%) had Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 1, and 37 (61%) had stage IVB cancer. All tumours were of adenocarcinoma histology and 18 (30%) patients had asymptomatic brain metastases at screening. At the time of the primary analysis (database cutoff Aug 26, 2024), median follow-up was 9·0 months (IQR 5·8-12·6) and 28 patients were still receiving the treatment combination. Objective response by 12 weeks was shown for 20 patients among the first 60 enrolled (objective response rate 33% [95·6% CI 21-47]), successfully rejecting an objective response rate of 20% or less. Overall, 24 of 61 (39% [95% CI 27-53]) patients showed partial response (22 confirmed at subsequent tumour evaluation). The most commonly reported TRAEs of any grade were infusion-related reaction (35 [58%] of 60 patients) and acneiform rash (30 [50%] of 60 patients). Treatment-related venous thromboembolism of any grade and grade 3-4 was reported in ten (17%) and two (3%) patients, respectively. No treatment-related deaths were observed. Grade 3-4 TRAEs occurred in 26 (43%) of 60 patients, with serious TRAEs observed in 12 (20%) of 60 patients.
sections.conclusion: Combined amivantamab, lazertinib, and bevacizumab showed durable anti-tumour activity, representing a promising chemotherapy-sparing alternative after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs. Safety was consistent with known toxicity profiles.

items.title: From discovery to proof: a Translation Evidence Map for precision psychiatry.
items.abstract: Precision psychiatry aims to improve individual-patient decisions by measuring clinically meaningful heterogeneity, not by privileging any one data type, biomarker, or analytical method. This Personal View proposes a Translation Evidence Map that stages claims, from Level 0 (defined use case or discovery-positioning statement) to Level 6 (post-deployment monitoring), linked to measurement reliability, generalisable inference, decision value, safe delivery, and proportionality to risk, clinical need, and inaction. The Map does not replace Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), biomarker qualification, prediction-model, regulatory, or roadmap frameworks; it identifies the highest defensible claim across components of unequal maturity and the next evidence step for compound precision claims. The Personal View discusses examples spanning inflammatory and circuit-based depression stratification, psychosis relapse monitoring, and suicidality monitoring, illustrating how the Map makes claim maturity, stopping points, stakeholder roles, and trade-offs important to patients explicit.

items.title: CAR T cells for autoimmune diseases: 2026 update of the EBMT-ISCT-JACIE practice harmonisation and consensus recommendations.
items.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are a heterogeneous group of chronic diseases characterised by loss of immune tolerance with substantial morbidity and mortality. Since 2021, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells have recently emerged as a promising treatment option for patients with severe, refractory autoimmune diseases. In 2024, an international expert panel from the European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation (EBMT), the International Society for Cell and Gene Therapy (ISCT), and the Joint Accreditation Committee of ISCT and EBMT (JACIE) released the first best-practice recommendations on CAR T cells for autoimmune diseases. Using the same consensus methodology, these living recommendations were updated thereafter. The 2026 consensus reviews current evidence and expert practices on CAR T cells for rheumatic, neurological, haematological, other autoimmune diseases, and paediatric indications, providing updated, expert-based recommendations on patient selection, diagnostic investigation, clinical management, follow up, and immune monitoring for each disease group. Unmet needs and future research priorities are also highlighted.

items.title: A heritability-optimized method for functional prioritization of rare coding variants in complex traits.
items.abstract: Population sequencing studies are uncovering millions of missense rare variants (RVs) implicated in the 'missing heritability' of complex diseases, yet distinguishing functional from neutral variation remains challenging. Here we present rare variant heritability-optimized scores (RovHer), a heritability-optimized method for inferring a variant's probability of being functional (that is, its contribution to trait variance). RovHer leverages exome-wide association statistics across 4,927,334 RVs and uses multivariate adaptive regression splines to integrate 75 variant- and gene-level features without a priori constraints. Across 21 traits in up to 357,086 UK Biobank European individuals, the top 1% of RovHer-prioritized missense RVs (m = 13,410) explained, on average, 16.1% of total RV heritability, a 10-fold gain over 7 alternative methods (average 1.5%; range 1.2-2.3%). RovHer's predictions are independent of allele frequency, generalize in a multi-ancestry replication and effectively identify high-risk carriers of severe clinical outcomes across 17 monogenic gene-trait pairs. Our tool showcases the value of missense RVs in population risk stratification.

items.title: Navigating global health futures under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways.
items.abstract: The Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) provide valuable insights to understand how future socioeconomic changes could alter the magnitude and pattern of climate-related risks across sectors, which might facilitate or hinder adaptation and mitigation responses. Many sectors have created SSP narrative extensions to specify insights for their domains. In this Viewpoint, we created health narrative extensions for the SSPs, considering socioeconomic and demographic drivers and population health and health-system drivers. The projected health-relevant trajectories diverge substantially over the course of the 21st century. The SSP3 and SSP4 narratives detail changes that could contribute considerable risks to health, whereas the SSP1 and SSP5 narratives highlight the role of effective governance and adequate resourcing in reducing climate-sensitive population health outcomes and health-system drivers. Given that climate forcing is considered exogenous to these narrative extensions, SSP5's favourable health driver paths do not account for the potential adverse impacts of this high-emissions pathway. The narratives elaborate population health drivers that can improve the policy relevance of population health and health-system risk projections associated with climate change across a range of possible pathways, and link these drivers with relevant cross-sectoral issues (eg, water and energy). Further research is required to quantify key drivers of population health and health-system risks at global to local scales.

items.title: Growth patterns of children with congenital Zika syndrome in Brazil: a matched-cohort study.

sections.objective: Children born with congenital Zika syndrome typically present with structural abnormalities and neurological impairments that can disrupt postnatal growth. We aimed to evaluate longitudinal anthropometric trajectories of children with congenital Zika syndrome compared with children without congenital Zika syndrome in Brazil.
sections.methods: In this matched-cohort study, we used Brazilian administrative data on singleton livebirths from Jan 1, 2015, to Dec 31, 2018, with follow-up routine primary care health data from birth to age 5 years. We excluded children with missing or inconsistent information about sex, type of pregnancy, birthweight, gestational age, date of birth, and anthropometric measurements. Cases of congenital Zika syndrome were obtained from the Brazilian Ministry of Health's Public Health Event Registry. For children classified with congenital Zika syndrome, we excluded those with a diagnosis of congenital syphilis or toxoplasmosis. An exactly matched comparison group of children with a similar likelihood of exposure to the Zika virus was selected. Descriptive statistics was used to compare anthropometric characteristics among children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly, children with congenital Zika syndrome without microcephaly, and children without congenital Zika syndrome. Using mixed-effects models, we estimated mean trajectories of length or height (cm), weight (kg), and BMI (kg/m 2 ) for these three groups. Multi-state models, stratified by microcephaly status and sex, were applied to compare transitions between nutritional status (based on WHO growth indicators) over time.
sections.results: We analysed growth measurements for 1268 children with congenital Zika syndrome and 6340 matched controls. Measurements indicative of stunting (length-for-age and height-for-age Z score <-2), underweight (weight-for-age Z score <-2), malnutrition (BMI-for-age Z score <-2), and wasting (weight-for-length and weight-for-height Z score <-2) were more frequent among children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly (1676 [49·2%] of 3408, 1623 [39·3%] of 4126, 743 [21·8%] of 3408, and 839 [24·6%] of 3408, respectively) and children with congenital Zika syndrome but no microcephaly (924 [30·5%] of 3028, 857 [24·0%] of 3577, 566 [18·7%] of 3028, and 602 [19·9%] of 3028, respectively) than among children without congenital Zika syndrome (3489 [11·0%] of 31 836, 1355 [3·5%] of 38 172, 1490 [4·7%] of 31 836, and 1410 [4·4%] of 31 836, respectively; all p<0·0001). At age 5 years, adjusted mean height was 6·61 cm less in children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly and 4·21 cm less in those without microcephaly than matched controls. In transition models, the 6-month probability of recovery from severe stunting (≥-6 SD to <-3 SD) among children with congenital Zika syndrome with microcephaly was 0·32 (95% CI 0·27-0·37) in males and 0·24 (0·20-0·29) in females. The transition probabilities increased among children with congenital Zika syndrome and no microcephaly (0·47 [95% CI 0·40-0·53] in males and 0·37 [0·30-0·44] in females). By contrast, the transition probabilities were at least 0·75 among all children without congenital Zika syndrome. Expected first passage times, representing the expected time to transition from one nutritional state to another, also indicated slower recovery in children with congenital Zika syndrome.
sections.conclusion: A substantial and persistent burden of growth impairment in children with congenital Zika syndrome highlights the need for sustained growth monitoring and targeted nutritional interventions to support long-term health in this population. For the Portuguese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: The public health challenges of children's and adolescents' digital media use: applying the digital determinants of health as an interpretive framework.
items.abstract: Children and adolescents are growing up in a hybrid world in which digital media has become part of the infrastructure of everyday life and a structural determinant of their health. In the second paper of this Series on the digital determinants of health, we apply the framework introduced in the first paper to one of the most contested questions in public health: how young people's digital media use shapes their health and wellbeing. Using the digital determinants of health framework to interpret the current evidence base, we examine what is known, and what remains poorly understood, about the public health implications of children's and adolescents' digital media use. Evidence suggests that digital media use can be associated with both benefits and harms although it is more consistently associated with adverse mental, behavioural, physical, cognitive, and social outcomes, with developmental stage emerging as an important moderator. Illustrative modelling indicates the potential population burden is substantial, even as its causal basis remains uncertain. Research to date has privileged easily measured proxies, such as screen time, and given insufficient attention to the platform design, algorithmic systems, and commercial incentives that shape young people's experiences. Situating young people's digital media use with a digital determinants of health framework, we conclude that protecting children's and adolescents' health calls for a precautionary, structural response-one that moves beyond individual behaviour change to reshape the digital systems, incentives, and knowledge practices that determine how digital media affects health.

items.title: Governing the digital determinants of health for children and young people: a global public health imperative.
items.abstract: The digital determinants of health are the structural conditions through which digital infrastructures, business models, and design choices shape health outcomes. Yet these determinants remain largely outside public health policy and remain fragmented across regulatory sectors. Rather than regulating individual technologies in isolation, governance should ensure that digital systems and environments advance population health and reduce inequities. A public health approach shifts attention from individual responsibility-and the tendency to blame users-towards the governance of the structural features that produce health risks and inequities. We identify four governance domains for the digital determinants of health: infrastructure and access, platform design and commercial practices, data governance and surveillance, and institutional accountability and rights. Effectively governing these domains requires intersectoral strategies that tackle problematic concentrations of political and economic power. We argue that the governance of the digital determinants of health should be recognised as a core public health function, with the health of children and young people as a priority and entry point and precaution as a guiding governance principle.

items.title: The digital determinants of health: a new era for global public health.
items.abstract: Digital transformations exert increasing influence over the lives of the global population, shaping opportunities and generating harms for health and wellbeing across the spectrum of digital access and engagement. The scale of influence of digital transformations on human and planetary health marks the urgency of attention to the digital determinants of health (DDoH). In this Series paper, we describe a prevailing digital sociotechnological order (DSTO) as the structural source of the DDoH. The DSTO is composed of a set of dominant assumptions that motivate digital practices operating through four features (political norms, economic logics, infrastructures, and personal and social practices) to affect human and planetary health. We describe the implications of the DSTO for understanding, studying, and governing the DDoH, and present recommendations for future work.

items.title: Accumulating Evidence Supports NECTIN4 as a Predictive Biomarker for Enfortumab Vedotin: The Compartment Still Matters.
items.abstract: Accumulating data support nectin-4, particularly membranous expression, as a predictive biomarker of enfortumab vedotin activity. Low expression identifies patients with poorer outcomes but not absence of benefit, underscoring the need for standardized prospective validation before clinical implementation.

items.title: PSMA-PET/CT-guided Intensification of Radiation Therapy for Prostate Cancer (PSMAgRT): 5-yr Analysis of a Phase 2 Randomized Controlled Trial.

sections.objective: Prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography (PSMA-PET) improves lesion detection, leading to treatment intensification via PSMA-guided radiotherapy (PSMAgRT), but its impact on patient outcomes remains undefined. We evaluated whether PSMAgRT improves failure-free survival (FFS).
sections.methods: This phase 2, two-center, open-label randomized trial enrolled patients planned for standard-of-care (SOC) radiotherapy (RT). Patients were randomized 1:1 to SOC or PSMAgRT to all detected sites across four strata: salvage post-radical prostatectomy (RP), high-risk, oligometastatic, and salvage post-RT. Between 2018 and 2021, 262 patients were randomized (253 treated/analyzed).
sections.results: The primary FFS end point (measured from RT completion) comprised prostate-specific antigen (PSA)/radiological progression, next-line therapy, or death. Secondary end points included freedom from biochemical progression (FFBP; PSA rise ≥0.2 ng/ml post-RP or ≥2 ng/ml above nadir in other strata).
